Unlike security requirements, they do not aim to prevent, detect, or recover from harm, and do not operationalise security policies. They may include functional requirements (which define what the system should do) and other non-functional requirements such as performance, usability, reliability, scalability, and maintainability. While they may influence system design and operation, they do not explicitly enforce security mechanisms or aim to mitigate security concerns.
